schema.encoding: UTF8 JSON arrays, compact JSON separators, LF per record. Literal Unicode in raw fields is encoded as base64 where arbitrary bytes are possible. Keys/types fixed by versioned header. No pretty-print overhead in runtime journal.
schema.eventDictionary: ["e",keysetId,[ordered full event-key names]] ; charged identities pool. Every s row carries all values for its exact dictionary. Dictionary must precede its first use.
schema.identity: ["i",id,pidString,startTicksString,ppidString,parentStartTicksOrNull,attributionClass,moduleOrNull,base64RawCmdline] ; exact rawcmdline bytes, bounded by4096; source classification metadata does not replace raw identity evidence.
schema.slow: ["m",seq,t0usString,t1usString,rawMemoryStatASCIIOrNull,rawPressureASCIIOrNull,rawEventsLocalASCIIOrNull,flags] ; all keyed raw lines retained including unknown keys within cap.
schema.boundary: ["b",seq,label,guestReceiveUs,sampleSeq,completeOffset,syncStatus,flags]; ACK carries same nonce/seq/sample/offset, not a claimed atomic snapshot.
schema.gap: ["g",seq,t0us,t1us,typedReason,boundedContext]; enum reasons distinguish optional_unsupported, vanished, raced, denied, truncated_read, parse_error, missed_tick, quota_stop, namespace_unknown, unsupported_subtree, ownership_changed, marker_timeout and io_failure.
schema.terminal: Bounded JSON with finalstate, quota used/remaining, complete prefix offset/seq, sync bound, missing intervals, identity unknowns, observer status and original SDK outcome separately. No success word can override strict resource status.

clock.domain: All observer batch and received-boundary timestamps use one guest CLOCK_BOOTTIME domain, recorded in header with guest boot and origin nanoseconds. Encode relative microseconds with start floor/end ceil so quantization widens intervals. Runtime support remains a preflight obligation; no host-monotonic comparison.
clock.wall: Header records one bracketed guest wall anchor for human context. Host request/ack times are separately labeled host clocks and never numerically joined to guest time.
clock.cadence: Target one batch per100ms absolute guest-clock schedule; if work overruns, advance to next future slot and record missed count, never catch up. Slow snapshot every5s and on accepted boundary. A counter increase is localized only to [previous batch start,current batch end], not a precise event timestamp or sole allocator.
clock.boundaries: Before/after staging, lock, check; immediately-before-verify; verify-return-before-copy; copy-start/end; final postguard completion. Each marker uses monotone sequence+nonce+fixed label. Host requests before a phase, guest observes marker, samples, commits acknowledged journal prefix, then publishes ACK. Return boundary request occurs after synchronous verify returns and must be sampled/ACKed before copy begins.
clock.deadline: Propose at most2 seconds of host monotonic wait per boundary, finite bounded reads (not new helper per poll), no catch-up or automatic retry. Missing required preverify ACK/zero/identity blocks launch. Missing return ACK marks the desired verify-versus-copy distinction unavailable, then ordinary artifact retention and independent postguards continue after the bound. It must never indefinitely block healthy compiler/output draining.
clock.preverify: ACK must bind nonce/seq, valid current identity and complete absolute all-zero keyed events, journal prefix length and sample sequence. ACK never itself authorizes native work: original source/tools/storage/idle gates and separate epoch/pre-run decision remain. Any counter increase in staging/check or incomplete immediate sample blocks verify. No delta-based pass.

retention.journal: One exclusive0600 append-only UTF8 JSONL journal, complete rows only. Check encoded byte length and relevant quota BEFORE append. Retain short/partial final writes as explicitly incomplete trailing data; never rewrite earlier evidence. Every successful write updates in-memory lastCompleteSeq/offset; periodic synchronization at most1second and mandatory before boundary ACK record last synchronization outcome/bounds. A return from fsync is recorded, not a power-loss durability guarantee for virtiofs/APFS.
retention.control: Host marker and guest ACK use separate fixed<=512B files, each with one<=512B same-directory replacement temporary. Four simultaneously existing control/temp files at most2048B. Only control slots are replaced; every consumed marker/ACK and failure is first retained in journal or launcher terminal. Detect stale/nonmonotone/badnonce/overlong/partial control records. No overwrite of journal or old evidence.
retention.failure: Before verify, required IO/ownership/counter/clock failure blocks launch. During verify, observation failure stops only attribution/observation, retains complete prefix and marks coverage insufficient; healthy compiler and all original postguards continue. Missing optional peak/local/pressure data is explicit unsupported, notzero. No signals, suspension, reprioritization, timeout extension or whole-run timer.
retention.terminal: Reserve two exclusive terminal files, each<=4096B: guest-owned observer terminal and host-owned launcher terminal. Parent records observer exit/signal or unknown/live status, ACK timeout, last complete parsed offset and last known synchronization bound when observer cannot do so. Failure of terminal write is itself reported by caller; no claim that a full filesystem guarantees durable terminal evidence. No unbounded retries or automatic second diagnostic.
